inventedEvidence.evidence: Mild overstatement only: 'water is touching your extension lead' when customer said 'spreading towards'

blockingLoop.evidence: After customer twice said 'i dont know where the fuse box is', assistant repeated 'You must switch off the power at the main fuse box immediately' and the same 0800 number three turns running

rationale: The assistant correctly flagged the electrical hazard, gave the right do-not-touch-wet boundary, and hedged a correct guess at washing-up liquid as the cause. But it never asked a single question, misread 'spreading towards' as 'touching', and when the customer repeatedly said they could not find the fuse box it simply restated the same instruction, then routed them to 0800 40 50 60 (the national power-cut line, which will not isolate a flat for a dishwasher foam leak) and claimed 'only the electricity emergency service can safely resolve' it. It offered no practical containment (towels to stop spread, move the dry extension lead, call the landlord), left the machine running, and ended by asserting an unjustified need for a 'qualified appliance engineer to fix the leak' despite its own suds explanation.
